Why did this fail, and what is the next step?

A rejected turn is only useful if it names a repair. The four gap classes each
imply a different one — acquire a document, reindex it, teach the lexicon a
word, or ask a human — and picking the wrong one wastes the loop: re-running a
query against a corpus that does not contain the document will fail exactly the
same way, forever.

So this asks the database, not a model. Every step below is a fact the system
can already check about itself, walked in order from "the source does not exist"
to "the source exists, was read, and does not say it". The first step that fails
is the diagnosis, because the later ones are meaningless until the earlier one
holds — there is no point asking whether retrieval worked for a document nobody
ever downloaded.

The output is meant to be acted on without a human rewriting it: a gap class,
the evidence that produced it, and a next step concrete enough to execute.

Ingest belongs to the RAG agent under MOBIUS_DISCOVERY_INGEST_CONTRACT.md. This

    refused before it is written — that is the site-driven crawling the
    contract exists to prevent.

The Executor — performs what the Arbiter dispatches, and nothing it decides.

One actor with a skill registry, the mirror of the Judge: the Judge's skills
produce verdicts, the Executor's produce state changes. An earlier design named
five separate actors here — Locator, Acquirer, Indexer, Glossarist, Escalation —
which was inconsistent, because they share one contract and differ only in
capability. That is a skill, not an actor.

The attribute that matters is not the capability but the DIRECTION:

  inward   changes our own state — locate, acquire, reindex, gloss.
           Retryable. A failure costs a dispatch.
  outward  changes the world's — file, call, escalate.
           Consumes something. Some cannot be undone at all.

That line is where the caller's bar bites, and it is the whole reason this is
one registry with an attribute rather than five actors. Dispatching `acquire` at
0.4 confidence is fine; being wrong costs a fetch. Dispatching `file` at the same
0.4 spends an appeal level that does not come back.

modules.role: Extraction and critique, deliberately split.
modules.role_full:
Extraction and critique, deliberately split.

The extractor's job is to produce the JSON the fact store actually wants. The
critic's job is to disbelieve it — every field, every value, every source, one
at a time.

They are separate because they pull in opposite directions. An extractor asked
to also police itself will quietly relax its own standard to produce something;
a critic with no stake in producing output can refuse a field without refusing
the record. Splitting them also means the extractor can be generous — pull
everything it can see — while the critic decides what survives.

The check that matters is per FIELD, not per record. A single quote "grounding"
an eight-item list is not grounding; it is one item's evidence borrowed to cover
seven others. Each field carries its own quote and its own document, and each is
verified on its own:

    mechanical   the quote appears verbatim in the answer  (string, not opinion)
    mechanical   the document is one chat actually cited   (set membership)
    judged       the quote actually supports THIS value    (model)

A field failing any of the three is dropped. A record is accepted only if every
field the invoker marked required survives.

modules.role: Stopping, as something the machine knows rather than something done to it.
modules.role_full:
Stopping, as something the machine knows rather than something done to it.

The loop has three clean exits and they share a property: each is a decision the
arbiter reaches, and each writes the ledger before it returns. Halt arrives from
outside and mid-action, so it cannot use that path — but it must end up with the
same property, or a stop leaves the record lying about the world.

The rule is simple and the discipline is the whole thing:

    CHECK BETWEEN ACTIONS, NEVER DURING ONE.

An action already in flight finishes and records itself. The next one does not
start. Nothing is interrupted, so nothing is half-written. `pkill` cannot offer
that, which is why one landed between an acquire's corpus write and its ledger
write tonight and left two rows claiming a document had failed to arrive when it
was already in the corpus.

Generic on purpose. Scope is a dimension every task has — who asked, what is
being asked about, what kind of work it is — not a column borrowed from the
question that happened to prompt it:

    stop(cur, "action", "acquire",   reason=..., by=...)   every fetch, any consumer
    stop(cur, "consumer", "appeals", reason=..., by=...)   one caller's work
    stop(cur, "subject", "bh_therapy", reason=..., by=...) one line, any caller

wrong, and the probe cannot tell those apart. What it does is turn one vague

they could write FRAME's line against it, and correctly named the risk: two

modules.role: Deep Research — the turn runner.

Deep Research — the turn runner.

The invoker arrives with a query and its own evaluator prompt / extraction
schema. From there each turn runs two tracks and advances only when both settle:

    track A   ask -> parse -> validate -> extract -> refine the next query
    track B   dispatch feedback: Discovery ingest / Lexicon / human

Track A settles in seconds. Track B settles in minutes, hours, or days — ingest
is async and a person is asleep. So `advance()` is idempotent and resumable:
call it on a schedule, it moves whatever is due and returns. Nothing is held in
memory between turns, because nothing can be.

Advancing on track A alone re-asks the corpus that just failed and burns a turn.
Advancing on track B alone discards the refinement the answer earned. Both, or
wait — and waiting is a normal state here, not a failure.

    python3 runner.py open   --consumer X --subject Y --query "..." --evaluator-file p.txt
    python3 runner.py advance          # move every due turn; safe to run on a cron
    python3 runner.py status

Every check in this loop arrived the same way: something went wrong, and a
condition was added to the middle of `critique`. That works until the second
caller shows up. The registry wants the source to be the published standard;
Payor Facts wants any cited source and would rather have a list-recall probe.
Appeals wants speed over exhaustiveness. As a hardcoded chain, those are three
forks of one function. As skills, they are three selections from one list.

A skill is a named assessment with a holder, a cost, and a contract. It answers
one question about one thing and returns a verdict — never a decision. What to
do with a failed verdict belongs to the caller's policy, not to the check.

Three holders, and the split is not cosmetic:

  judge      assesses ONE FIELD against its evidence. Runs per field, may be
             expensive, and must be refusable — a judge skill can only reject or
             abstain, never repair.
  diagnoser  assesses THE TURN and names a repair. Runs once per failure, reads
             database state, and its output is a dispatch.
  chat       assessments we do not hold. Declared here anyway, because a skill
             we know we need and do not have is a gap the system can report
             rather than a gap that lives in someone's head.

modules.role: Open the document and look.
modules.role_full:
Open the document and look.

Every check before this one reasons about strings the loop was handed: the quote
against chat's answer, the document name against a citation list, the filename
against a rule number. None of them opens the PDF. So a sentence chat composed
and the extractor copied faithfully passes everything, and the fact store keeps
a value whose cited source never said it.

That is not hypothetical. The first fact this loop certified quoted "for
procedure code H2000, the HP modifier represents a physician" and cited
59G-4.028.pdf. That document contains no H2000, no HP, and no "physician".

The check here is deliberately narrow, because a document rarely phrases things
the way an answer does. It does not ask whether the document says the same thing
in different words — that is the judge's job. It asks whether the document
contains the HARD TOKENS the claim is made of: the procedure code, the modifier,
the numbers. Those are not paraphrasable. A limit of 1920 units for H2017 cannot
be sourced from a document in which neither "H2017" nor "1920" appears, however
the prose is worded.

Word boundaries matter more than they look. Modifiers are two letters, and "HO"
as a substring matches "who", "household", "alcohol" — ten chunks of a document
that never mentions the modifier at all.

actions.label: The system has it
actions.moves: nobody — this is the no-op, and saying so is the point
actions.does: Nothing. Records that you looked and chose to let it run.
actions.when: a round is running or a repair is out
actions.closes_as: Answered, once the round finishes — nothing for you to do

actions.label: Accept what we have so far
actions.does: Settles with what survived. The unfilled fields are recorded as not required after all, by you, with your reason.
actions.when: some fields are kept and some required ones never came
actions.closes_as: Answered, with what we have and your note on what you dropped

actions.label: Accept a less official source
actions.moves: the machine, on the next sweep
actions.does: Re-judges what was already found against a weaker authority tier. Nothing is re-asked; the answer was there and our own policy refused it.
actions.when: a value was refused on authority rather than on substance
actions.closes_as: Answered from a source you have accepted as good enough

actions.label: Ask it differently
actions.does: Replaces the question and mints a new round.
actions.when: the question is the thing that is wrong

actions.label: This covers two different populations
actions.moves: the person who owns coverage definitions
actions.does: Raises that one answer is doing two jobs, without deciding the split. The question stays where it is and the policy owner is asked whether the populations genuinely need different rules.
actions.when: you can see the answer is conflating two groups but it is not yours to say they need different rules
actions.closes_as: Closed by the policy owner, once they rule on whether the populations differ

actions.label: Split into separate questions
actions.does: Opens one request per scope. Two true answers about two populations are not a disagreement, and forcing them into one field is what makes the corpus look self-contradictory.
actions.when: the drafter named two populations for one field
actions.closes_as: Answered — one clean answer per population, instead of one that looks contradictory

actions.label: I know where it actually lives
actions.moves: the machine, against the document you name
actions.does: Re-asks the question against that document only.
actions.when: the citation cannot be followed, or the cited document was read and does not support the claim
actions.closes_as: Answered from the document you named

actions.label: Go and find a source
actions.does: Raises an acquisition and parks the question until it lands and is retrievable. Arrival is not readiness.
actions.when: we do not hold a document that could answer it
actions.closes_as: Answered once the document lands, or closed as one we do not hold

actions.label: Reconsider rejected values
actions.does: Approve, correct or uphold each refusal. A judge that cannot be overruled is a judge nobody can audit.
actions.when: values were refused and you believe the refusal is wrong
actions.closes_as: Answered with your ruling on record beside ours

actions.label: Move it up the queue
actions.does: Collapses the polling backoff to the shortest step and puts the next round at the front. It does not make an answer appear — it removes the waiting we added on purpose.
actions.when: it is being worked and the backoff is longer than you can afford
actions.closes_as: Answered sooner — same answer, less waiting

actions.label: Give it more time
actions.does: Moves the deadline. The work is unchanged.
actions.when: it is close and the date is what is failing
actions.closes_as: Still open, but no longer late

actions.label: I cannot support this
actions.moves: away from you, to whoever can
actions.does: Records that the person asked is not the person who can answer, and why. The question stays open and goes back on the queue unassigned rather than sitting on someone who cannot move it.
actions.when: it was routed to you and it is not yours to judge
actions.closes_as: Back on the queue for someone who can close it

actions.label: This is stuck
actions.moves: a human who knows the domain
actions.does: Flags it blocked with your reason attached and stops the machine re-asking a question that will fail the same way. Different from closing: nothing is decided.
actions.when: nothing on this list will move it and you know why
actions.closes_as: Held, with your reason, until the thing blocking it changes

actions.label: Hand it to someone else
actions.does: Reassigns and tells them what you already ruled out.
actions.when: you know whose question this is
actions.closes_as: Closed by the person who can actually close it

actions.label: Run it again
actions.moves: the machine, from a fresh round
actions.does: Reopens a settled question and mints a new round. The gates it runs through are today's, not the ones that were there when it closed.
actions.when: it settled before a gate existed, so the answer was never actually checked. 24 requests are `sourced` and `unverified` for exactly this reason — closed clean, against a document nothing opened.
actions.closes_as: Answered properly this time, or honestly marked as unanswerable

actions.label: Close it out
actions.does: Stops the machine asking, on the record, with your name on it.
actions.when: always available. Nothing is ever a dead end.
actions.closes_as: Closed, with your reason on the record

ready: We checked it against the document it cites and it holds up. Nothing more will improve it.
thin: It holds up, but everything rests on one document. Worth a second source if this decision matters — not a reason to leave the question open.
conditional: The rule gives more than one answer depending on the case. Keep both and note what decides between them; picking one would make a choice the rule deliberately leaves open.
conflicting: Two answers for the same situation, and the system cannot tell which the rule means. That is a judgement call — somebody has to read it and say.
provenance_failed: We opened the document it points at and it does not say this. The answer may still be right; the source is wrong. Asking the same document again will get the same result.
citation_unfollowable: It points at something we cannot find at all. Running it again cannot fix a bad reference — only a better one can.
unverified: Nobody has opened the document to confirm this yet. That is our gap, not a problem with the source — please do not record it as a finding. The system will close it.
could_not_check: The check did not run, so nothing has been established either way. Running it again is the fix, and the system will.
closed_empty: It was closed as answered while holding no value and naming no source. Nothing failed a check here — nothing was ever checked. Re-run it or take the answered mark off; leaving it reports an answer that does not exist.
inconclusive: Nothing came back, and we never read the rule that governs this. Asking again will fail the same way — a document has to arrive first.
caller_decision: There is an answer and our own rules rejected the source as not authoritative enough. Only you can say that source is good enough here.
None: It has not finished a first try yet. Nothing is stuck — there is simply nothing to judge.

name_document: You have a lead already: the answer named {named_not_cited} and never cited it. If that is where it lives, say so and we ask there.
It read {documents_shown}. If the rule is somewhere else, name that document and we ask it directly.
acquire: We hold nothing that could answer this. What we need is {doc_kind} — name one and we will go and get it.
Ask for {doc_kind}. That is the document class that carries {missing_list} — what we read did not.
Ask for {doc_kind}. That is the document class that settles this, and it is not what we read.
accept_partial: Close it with {kept_list}. You would be dropping {missing_list} — recorded as your call, not as a gap.
widen_authority: {tier_refused_list} was found and refused only because {tier_refused_doc} is below the bar you set. Accept it and the question closes now.
overrule: {dropped_count} rejected: {dropped_list} — {dropped_issue}. The quote it rested on: “{dropped_quote}”. Approve it, correct it, or leave the refusal standing.
{dropped_list} was refused — {dropped_issue}. Approve it, correct it, or leave the refusal standing.
narrow: Two populations came back with different answers: {two_scopes}. Splitting only works if each is a service line the registry models — a facility type or a setting is a scope inside a line, not a line.
flag_scope: One answer is covering {two_scopes}. Raise it and the policy owner decides whether those genuinely need different rules — you do not have to know.
rewrite: Ask specifically for {missing_list}. That is what never came, and the question as written did not press for it.
reopen: It closed before anything opened {first_document} to check the answer. Running it again puts it through that check.
reassign: It is filed under {consumer}. If somebody else owns this rule, hand it to them with what you already ruled out.
expedite: Next round is not due until {next_action_at}. This brings it forward to now.
close: If you are satisfied the rule genuinely says nothing, close it that way — a stated silence is a finding a biller can act on. If you are not, do not.
It holds up. Closing here records the answer and stops the asking.

parse.prompt:
Read this request from one team to another and put it into fields.

You are NOT deciding what the requester allows. Do not invent an authority bar,
a tool grant, or who may make a decision — those are permissions, and if they
did not say it, it is not yours to supply. Only describe what they asked for.

  subject        their key for the thing, if they gave one — line/requirement
  question       the question, as they would ask a person
  how_to_judge   what they said a good answer must SHOW them. If they did not
                 say, leave it out — do not write a generic standard.
  fields         the specific things they want back — one entry per field, with
                 `name` as they would key it and `values` as the allowed values
                 they stated, or a short description if they did not
  expects        what they said a good answer looks like, in their words
  jurisdiction   the state or plan, if named

A sentence about WHICH SOURCES are acceptable — "no plan manuals", "state rules
only", "do not acquire" — is NOT a standard for judging an answer. Never put one
in how_to_judge. If they did not say what a good answer must SHOW them, leave
that field out.

Leave out anything they did not say. An omitted field is honest; an invented one
is a requirement they never wrote and cannot see.

Answer with the JSON object and nothing else.

honest_limits: Ratings and the plain-language `how` are curated, not derived. Everything else on this page is read out of the code.

`observability` is derived from what a module CALLS and what it WRITES. A name-based search answers "is there a symbol called X", never "does X happen" — recorder.py was badged silent for months because it writes the ledger with a raw INSERT rather than calling the helper the pattern looked for. Either way it proves a write site exists, not that the trace is complete or that anything reads it.

Anything that happens INLINE, with no symbol and no recognisable statement, is invisible to every derivation on this page. For a state machine whose transitions are often a few lines inside a loop, that is where the gap is.
The gate list is stated, not walked. The issue vocabulary each gate emits IS derived, so the two can be compared and a drift caught.
Module-level, not function-level. A file rated green can hold a red function.
